title: plan 0040's handset leg. The PANEL-FIT half is now answered and did not need hardware: the longest string this screen draws is the ARMED prompt, not a label, and "OK again: reboot to fastboot" was 28 columns on a 26-column panel — it shipped truncated to "OK again: reboot to fastbo". Fixed (the two cable rows' verbs are `fastboot`/`EDL`), pinned by a golden that arms row 3, and guarded by `wata-fb exitfit` in the fb smoke. What is LEFT is only what fingers can do: open the menu on the handset, take `Restart app` and `Reboot` for real, and walk fastboot/EDL as far as the SECOND prompt without confirming. It cannot be driven from here — the device has no /dev/uinput and the app opens /dev/input/event0..2, which are the three real keypads, so there is no way to inject a keypress over ssh. The installed binary is current as of 2026-08-08 10:49 and has the exit menu in it
blocked: needs the owner's fingers on the handset (no uinput; app reads event0..2 only)

title: the `-page_duration 20000` flag in tools/make-chirp.py is now INERT and should go at the next regeneration. It existed because the old reader took a page's payload as one frame, so an ffmpeg-default chirp read as a single oversized frame; Ogg.readFrames walks the lacing table now and the asset would be correct without it. It cannot simply be deleted: the asset is committed as BYTES and `--check` has to keep reproducing them, so the flag comes out only when the chirp is next re-encoded from the owner's source recording (which lives on the owner's machine only). Nothing breaks meanwhile — this is a tidy-up whose trigger is someone else's file
